framing.lineOfInquiry: Divya Malhotra (P00045) may have been involved in the incident recorded in CASE024
framing.alternate: Divya Malhotra (P00045) was not involved — the evidence has an innocent explanation
framing.note: KRONOS starts from the presumption of innocence. The line of inquiry and the alternates are tested against the same records; neither is a finding, and the strengths are not probabilities.

alternateHypotheses.title: Named or given a role in error
alternateHypotheses.statement: Divya Malhotra was named in the FIR, or assigned a role, without an independent basis.
alternateHypotheses.label: Strong
alternateHypotheses.test: Re-examine the FIR and statements; record the person's statement and the informant's basis for naming them.

alternateHypotheses.title: Was elsewhere at the time (alibi)
alternateHypotheses.statement: Divya Malhotra was somewhere else when the incident happened.
alternateHypotheses.label: Moderate

alternateHypotheses.statement: The flagged money movements of Divya Malhotra have an ordinary purpose (salary, rent, property, business) or belong to a co-holder of the account.
alternateHypotheses.label: Moderate

alternateHypotheses.title: The contact was routine, not coordination
alternateHypotheses.statement: Divya Malhotra's calls and messages reflect a long-standing relationship (family, work, business), not planning of the incident.
alternateHypotheses.label: Moderate

alternateHypotheses.title: Was near the scene for a routine reason
alternateHypotheses.statement: Divya Malhotra was near the scene because they regularly go there (home, work, market), not because of the incident.
alternateHypotheses.label: Weak

evidence.text: Recorded within 1 km of the scene on 38 other days (16 Mar – 10 May), so presence there is part of their routine

alternateHypotheses.test: Establish why the person is regularly there (address, employment, shop) and compare the incident-time visit with their usual pattern (time of day, duration).

alternatesConsideredNotSupported.title: Someone else used the phone or handset

comparison.verdict: Every supporting item could be explained by at least one alternate, although the line of inquiry is stronger on weight (0.84 vs 0.62). Test the alternates before relying on it.
settleWith: A6 — Re-examine the FIR and statements; record the person's statement and the informant's basis for naming them.
A1 — Verify the alibi record independently (CCTV, witnesses or receipts at that place and time) and check whether the device could have been carried by someone else.
A4 — Obtain full statements, invoices or agreements and KYC; confirm the stated purpose with the counter-party.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Divya Malhotra (P00045) was involved in the incident recorded in CASE024
hypotheses.name: Divya Malhotra

contradicting.text: record(s) 23.8 km away from the incident location within 3 h of the incident (Laxmi Nagar Residential, Delhi)

alternativeExplanations: Being named in an FIR records an allegation; it is not itself proof of involvement.
Flagged transactions may have legitimate explanations (business payments, loans, property, salary) — verify documents.
Frequent contact may reflect family, business or social ties unrelated to the incident.

confidence.note: Evidential balance compares weighted supporting vs contradicting evidence; it is not a probability of guilt. Prior records are excluded from this score.

note: Each hypothesis is tested from both sides to reduce confirmation bias. Confidence scores are evidential balance (not probability of guilt). Human review is required.
